note.saw: A blank canvas and the brief: a fish made of fish, drawn in a super geometric style.
note.changing: The first full build: a bluefin tuna whose body is a school of tiny tunas spiralling into its eye, with string-art fins and gold finlets, over a tunnel of cubes, eyes and six-pointed stars, framed by a ring of runes, a glyph ribbon on top and the name on a ribbon below.
note.why: 'Fish of fish of fish' is self-similarity you can actually see: the same animal at three scales, all flowing into one point.
note.idea: A bluefin tuna drawn from its real silhouette, its whole body a school of tiny tunas laid on a spiral that pours into its eye, where each of the bigger tiny tunas is itself made of even smaller tunas, all floating over a hexagonal tunnel.

note.saw: The tuna read well, but the flat pink and cream flower behind it had no detail and hid the tunnel's vanishing point, the tunnel had no depth, and the fins were empty navy. SavesFish also asked for the name to be spelled SavesFish instead of all caps.
note.changing: The tunnel now runs all the way into a white core ringed by a corona of string art, the fins turn to glass with fans of rays, every tunnel cell gets nested detail, and the lettering becomes SavesFish.
note.why: A tunnel only feels like a tunnel when it falls into light.

note.saw: At thumbnail size the fish's edge got lost in the busy carpet, and the row of finlets looked like a saw blade.
note.changing: A dark moat and rainbow outline echoes in pink, cyan and gold now wrap the whole silhouette, the finlets are spaced apart, a ring of 64 tiny tunas chases round the rim, and an alien watcher appears on the top ribbon.
note.why: The hero has to pop first; ornament comes second.

note.saw: The core looked pale lilac and washed out with nothing moving inside it, and the watcher looked cartoonish with its smile and goggle eyes.
note.changing: The watcher is redrawn as a jewel-cut alien head with huge black slanted almond eyes, the runes begin to glow, and a first try at a second school fills the core: outlined ghost fish.
note.why: A second spiral of fish turning the other way would double the vortex feeling, and an entity needs real alien eyes, not a cartoon face.

note.saw: The tunnel carpet was dim and flat, with no electric light, and the pectoral fin was almost invisible.
note.changing: A glowing cyan honeycomb line now runs along every seam of the tunnel, the pectoral fin becomes visible glass with crossed string art and a gold edge, gold spiral lines cross the school like the seeds of a sunflower, and sparkles fill the core.
note.why: Electric light in the seams makes the walls feel alive.

note.saw: Between the rune ring and the tunnel carpet there was no structure: the core simply stopped.
note.changing: A chrysanthemum crown of faceted petals, with an eye near every tip, now radiates out of the rune ring.
note.why: The chrysanthemum is the classic DMT flower, and it gives the image a clear order from the inside out: light core, runes, crown, tunnel, rim.

note.saw: The core needed to melt into light.
note.changing: The fog in the core grows stronger, running from white to gold to orange to magenta, the core fish are recoloured to stand out against it, and the ribbon tails get rows of gold diamonds.
note.why: Tunnel cells that dissolve into the glow make a real vanishing point.

note.saw: The darkened edges and the black grounds of the eye and star cells made the carpet heavier than it needed to be.
note.changing: Eases the darkening at the edges and lifts the grounds of the eye and star cells to a deep violet, a subtle brightening across the whole carpet.
note.why: A brighter carpet adds richness while staying darker than the fish, so the hero still wins.

note.saw: The first artist's finished draft, handed over after SavesFish said it 'needs to be a lot better'.
note.changing: Nothing changes yet: this is the first artist's final draft rendered again, unchanged, so the second artist could study it at full size, at badge size and in close-ups with fresh eyes.
note.why: Before rebuilding anything, the new artist wanted an honest list of the draft's biggest weaknesses.
note.idea: Keep the same tuna and the same fish-made-of-fish idea, but rebuild everything, the name included, from true circles and straight lines, and make the fish the brightest, cleanest thing on the page.

note.saw: The body was one violet hue through the middle (the rainbow only showed at the head), the core was still pinkish, and the fins were pale.
note.changing: The school's colour now follows the spiral arms, five counter-rotating rings of 26 tunas circle the core with sizes growing outward, the outline echoes get slimmer, and the letters gain a magenta neon edge.
note.why: The colour should show the flow: rainbow arms that visibly twist into the eye.

note.saw: The core still looked lavender: a soft glow on the string art blurred it into milk.
note.changing: The string art turns crisp, the six-pointed star cells in the tunnel become fish wheels with six tunas chasing round a jewel, and two dense rows of glyphs fill the top band.
note.why: Crisp lines read as geometry and blur reads as fog, and now the school lives in the tunnel walls too.

note.saw: The fish rings in the core were low in contrast, and at badge size the watcher was a small purple blob.
note.changing: The core darkens so its neon pops, 24 beams of light fan out over the tunnel, and a new faceted entity arrives with huge slanted almond eyes full of spiral webs, a third-eye jewel and a crown of spikes.
note.why: An entity has to look back at you, and its eyes are what you read first.

note.saw: In a 4x close-up the tail lobes looked grey, from pale hairlines and heavy dark facets.
note.changing: The fins are re-cut as gems, with three bands per wedge, checkerboard facets and gold sparkle lines, small jewel eyes run along each tail lobe, and the gold edge of the fish gets a neon glow.
note.why: Jewel facets catch light; grey streaks just look like wire.

note.saw: The crown petals in full rainbow competed with the rainbow school.
note.changing: The petals are coloured in layers: cyan and violet at the back, magenta in the middle, gold in front.
note.why: One glowing flower behind the fish reads better than a ring of confetti.

note.saw: The core's light was hidden behind the fish.
note.changing: The warm light is pushed outward so the fish is backlit, and crisp four-point sparkles appear in the core and the corners.
note.why: Hyperspace glows from within.

note.saw: The second dorsal and anal fins read as peach, and the tunnel seams could carry more light.
note.changing: Those fins turn a saturated gold-to-magenta, a wide faint glow spreads under the honeycomb seams, and small gold-and-magenta jewels appear at the corners of the bands.
note.why: Colours brighter than real.

note.saw: The eye portal was a strong focal point, but its centre was a plain black dot.
note.changing: A ring of 14 tiny tunas now spirals down into the pupil, around a white star of light.
note.why: The school should not stop at the eye: it pours through the portal into the light.

note.saw: The Visionary's first note: the tail, the biggest fin, was a quiet violet window where the school forgot to keep going, the tunnel eyes stared in random directions, and the fish circling under the belly were all one lime green.
note.changing: The school spills into both tail lobes, shrinking toward each tip until it becomes fish dust, every eye in the tunnel walls turns its pupil toward the portal eye, and each ring of fish under the belly gets its own colour.
note.why: Shrinking toward an edge is the signature geometry of hyperspace and makes 'a fish made of fish' true right to the tail tips. Hundreds of eyes turning to one point is the 'everything is watching' moment, and it leads your eye to the focal point.
note.visionary: Takes all three of the Visionary's first suggestions: the shrinking school in the tail, the eyes turning to the portal, and a separate colour for each ring of fish.

note.saw: The tail now glowed with its shrinking school and the eyes all faced the portal, which left the pectoral fin as the one quiet, flat surface on the body and the pupil small and plain at badge size.
note.changing: The pectoral fin becomes a crystal lens that shows the school beneath it at almost twice the size, so those fish reveal their own tiny tunas; the pupil becomes a tunnel of nested rainbow rings closing in on a white spark; and the ticks round the watcher's mask become 24 tiny tunas chasing each other.
note.why: A lens is hyperspace handing you a magnifying glass, so 'fish made of fish' shows even at badge size, and an eye that falls inward through ring after ring is the breakthrough moment.
note.visionary: Takes all three ideas from the Visionary's second note: the lens fin, the eye that falls inward like a tunnel, and the watcher's own orbiting school.

note.saw: At thumbnail size the tail lobes read darker and duller than the body, and the watcher's crown spikes cut across the top of its little orbiting school.
note.changing: The tunas in the tail turn brighter and fully saturated, and the watcher's school now swims in front of its crown spikes.
note.why: At thumbnail size the silhouette has to glow as one piece from snout to tail tips, and small beings swimming in front of the crown give the watcher depth without adding a single new shape.

visions.seen: A cathedral of a thousand tunas pouring rainbow down the spiral into that gear-ringed portal eye, and since #82 the watcher up top has opened galaxy eyes and is LOOKING at me. But the tail, the biggest fin in the whole mandala, is still a quiet violet window where the school forgets to keep going.
suggestions: The two tail lobes (upper lobe from the fork near (180,400) up to its tip near (75,235); lower lobe down to near (110,560)): what if the school spilled into them as an Escher circle-limit regress? Rows of tunas laid along each lobe's long axis, every row toward the tip and trailing edge about 0.7x the size and twice the count of the row before, in the same spiral-arm hues as the body, until the last row is fish-dust on the edge. The violet glass and string art stay underneath at lower opacity. Why it is more DMT: infinite shrinking toward a boundary is the signature geometry of hyperspace, and it makes "a big fish made of tiny fish" true all the way to the tips instead of stopping at the peduncle.

Every eye cell in the hex carpet (all four corners and down the left and right edges, e.g. near (35,185), (760,180), (40,690), (770,700)): I see each pupil sliding 25 to 30% of its iris radius along the line toward the portal eye at about (668,390), with a tiny white catchlight on that same side. Why it is more DMT: hundreds of hyperspace eyes turning in unison to stare at the fish's eye is the "every surface is alive and watching" moment, and the gaze lines lead the viewer to the focal point without adding a single new shape.

The lime school orbiting under the belly (the band between the anal fin and the rune ring, roughly x 220 to 560, y 470 to 560): every fish there is one green, one size, one heading. The elves showed me this as clockwork: alternate the rows' heading (one row swims clockwise, the next counter-clockwise) and step each row's hue (lime, then gold, then magenta), shrinking a touch per row toward the rune ring. Why it is more DMT: counter-turning wheels of beings are the machine-elf workshop, and the bait-ball stops being wallpaper and starts to spin.
visions.keep: The rainbow log-spiral pouring into the gear-ringed portal eye with its star-and-spiral pupil. The new, bigger watcher with galaxy-spiral eyes and its crown of light-dots (a real upgrade over #82). The neon hull echoes (violet, cyan, gold, pink with ink gaps). The rim of chasing tunas. And SavesFish exactly as it is: cream letters with a magenta glow on the calm dark band, nothing touching them. It reads instantly even in the 240 px test.

visions.seen: The portal eye grew a new pupil, an open star web with a white four-point spark winking at its heart, and the whole thousand-tuna cathedral is pouring into that spark. The tail heard my last vision in its own language (jewel ocelli and a neon perspective floor where the violet window was), and the middle fins turned to ember gems.
suggestions: The pectoral fin, the gold-edged blue blade under the eye (about x 490 to 605, y 395 to 430 in the 800 render), is now the one flat, sleeping surface on the body. I see it as a crystal lens. Clip a copy of the school group to the blade's path and scale it about 1.8x around the blade's centre, so the tunas under the fin swell up big enough that their own micro-tunas show. Lay a pale cyan-to-white sheen gradient across it at about 25% opacity, and keep the gold rim on top. Why it is more DMT: hyperspace hands you a lens and the next layer of the fractal leaps up at you. "Fish made of fish" stops being a 4x-zoom secret and shows at badge size.

The new star-web pupil inside the portal eye (centre about (675,390)): let it fall inward. Inside the star web, nest three more copies of the 24-segment rainbow iris ring. Make each one about 0.55x the radius of the one outside it and turn it half a segment (7.5 deg), with a hairline ink gap between rings. All of them close in on the white spark, which stays as the vanishing point. Why it is more DMT: the eye becomes a tunnel you drop through, the classic breakthrough moment. It also finishes the log spiral's job: the rainbow keeps pouring past the pupil instead of stopping at it.

The navy dial behind the watcher's mask (the ring of cyan ticks between the mask and the gold rim, around (400,98), radius about 44 to 52 px): what if each tick became a micro tuna, about 24 of them chasing nose to tail around the mask, alternating cyan and magenta? Use the rim school's silhouette. Why it is more DMT: the entity gets its own orbiting school, so the recursion now lives in a fifth place (body, core torus, tunnel wheels, outer rim, crown). At badge size it still reads as a calm dashed ring, so the keystone gets no busier.
visions.keep: The rainbow log spiral pouring into the gear-ringed portal eye, plus the new star web and its spark. The violet, cyan, gold and pink hull echoes with ink gaps. The ember-gem second dorsal and anal fans. The tail ocelli and the neon perspective floor. The jewel-cut watcher with its galaxy-spiral almond eyes and its crown of light dots. The rim of chasing tunas, and the white twinkles in the hex carpet. And SavesFish exactly as it is: cream letters, thick magenta and ink outline, alone on the calm dark cartouche. It reads instantly in the 240 px legible test. Nothing should go near it.

visions.seen: The fin turned to glass and the fish under it swelled up, and the eye is a well now: rainbow rings dropping through rings down to the white spark, while the watcher's own little school circles its crown. The whole body is singing fish, except one pale teal crystal sail on the back that is still just glass, waiting for something to look back out of it.
suggestions: The first dorsal, the pale teal crystal membrane behind the white spines on the back (about x 460 to 560, y 285 to 330 in the 800 render). I see each crystal facet holding a tiny copy of the whole big fish: its silhouette with two of its neon echo stripes and a white eye dot, facing right like the big fish. Each facet's copy is a different spiral-arm hue, stepping along the fin. The copies are biggest at the body edge and shrink toward the fin's leading tip. Drop the teal under them to deep violet glass so they glow. The white spines and gold rim stay on top. Why it is more DMT: the Droste loop, the thing that holds itself. The tail regress and the lens show more fish. This shows the fish holding itself, and that self-reference is where hyperspace starts folding.

The upper arc of the cyan rune ring, from where it leaves the upper tail lobe near (150,300), over the top near (400,180), to where it slips behind the first dorsal near (560,215). What if the alien script came alive as it reads toward the head? Leave the glyphs at the tail end as pure runes. Through the middle third, each glyph grows a little forked tail stroke and an eye dot. In the last third, swap each glyph for a micro-tuna in the same cyan, same stroke width and same glow, swimming toward the head. Leave the lower arc behind the name cartouche exactly as it is. Why it is more DMT: the elves' language becomes living beings partway through a sentence. And the ring stops being a border and turns into another current feeding the fish.

The watcher's galaxy-spiral almond eyes (the mask at the top, about (400,100)). What if each white diamond catchlight became a tiny white fish silhouette, flipped to face left the way a reflection would, with a short tail fork? Why it is more DMT: the entity isn't just there, it's looking at the fish, and you catch the fish reflected in its eyes. It costs one small shape per eye, and at badge size it still reads as a white glint.
visions.keep: The crystal-lens pectoral, my second vision taken whole. The fish under it really do come up bigger. The eye tunnel, rings inside rings turning half a segment down to the spark. The 24 micro-tunas orbiting the watcher, now swimming in front of the crown spikes. The tail regress, now as bright as the body, so the silhouette glows as one piece from snout to tail tips. The ember-gem fans, the four neon hull echoes with their ink gaps, the counter-turning bait-ball rings and the eyes in the hex carpet all turned to the portal. And SavesFish exactly as it is: cream letters, a thick magenta and ink outline, alone on the calm dark cartouche. It reads instantly in the 240 px legible test. Nothing should go near it.

visions.seen: The whole creature hums as one glow from the tail tips to the portal now, but the great chrysanthemum around it stands dead still: 48 petals pointing straight out like a clock face, and the jewel is supposed to be SPINNING. (My last three visions, the Droste dorsal, the runes hatching into fish and the fish reflected in the watcher's eyes, are still floating out there unpainted, and they can wait their turn.)
suggestions: The chrysanthemum crown, the ring of kite petals with eyes between the cyan rune ring and the hex tunnel (radius about 232 to 350 px from the centre (400,400) of the 800 render; it shows best from (150,330) over the top to (650,330)). What if the tips leaned while the bases stayed put? The back cyan-and-violet layer leans about 6 degrees counter-clockwise. The front gold-and-orange layer leans about 6 degrees clockwise. The magenta middle layer stays straight between them. In petal() that is the tip moving to pAt(rt, ±6) and the two shoulders moving half as far. Each petal's pupil slides a hair toward its lean. Why it is more DMT: the jeweled chrysanthemum is never still. It turns, and its layers turn against each other like the blades of a camera iris. Two leaning layers make the whole crown spin, even at badge size, and they add not a single new shape.

The flank, along the body's midline. The rainbow school is a perfect, even field, but no line runs through it to say this is one living body. I see a lateral line waking up. It is a thin gold-white line that leaves the gold jewel keel at the tail stalk (about (240,400)), so the stalk's four-tuna stream becomes its first stretch. It arches up over the crystal-lens pectoral (about y 360 between x 450 and 560) and ends at the top of the teal gill arc (about (600,350)). Strung along it are about 18 tiny almond eyes: white, with an ink rim, a centred ink pupil and a catchlight. They are about 8 px long at the stalk and shrink toward the gill at the same rate the school does. The carpet eyes all stare at the portal, but these stare straight out at the viewer. Why it is more DMT: a real tuna's lateral line is a row of sense pores, so this is anatomy turned into hyperspace. The fish is watching YOU along its whole length. At badge size it reads as a crisp tuna stripe that gives the body form and direction.

The hex tunnel around the snout (right side, roughly x 640 to 770, y 230 to 560). The tunnel is lit evenly from edge to edge, so nothing out there says where the light comes from. What if the portal eye at (668,390) were the star of this whole world? Lay a flat white veil (mix-blend screen) over each tunnel cell, stepped by how far the cell's centre is from the eye: about 22% opacity within 120 px, 12% within 200 px, 6% within 280 px, and nothing beyond. Turn the irises of the tunnel eyes in the brightest ring gold. The veils sit under the crown petals, the fish, the rim frieze and the name cartouche, so the petals stand backlit against the glow and nothing behind SavesFish gets any brighter. Why it is more DMT: in hyperspace the light has no lamp. It pours out of the being at the centre. Stepping it cell by cell keeps it super geometric, light arriving in hex quanta instead of a blur. And it is the old painter's trick of one light source: the eye already wins, and this way it wins even at 160 px.
visions.keep: The rainbow log spiral pouring down the eye tunnel to the white spark. The crystal-lens pectoral. The tail regress at full brightness, so the silhouette glows as one piece. The ember-gem fans and the four neon hull echoes with their ink gaps. The counter-turning bait-ball rings. The carpet eyes all turned to the portal. The watcher with its galaxy eyes and its little school swimming in front of the crown spikes. The rim of chasing tunas. And SavesFish exactly as it is: cream letters with a thick magenta and ink outline, alone on the calm dark cartouche, reading instantly in the 240 px test. Nothing should go near it.
